unchanged_original_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact reduced locally irreducible (unibranch) complex space of pure complex dimension n, with a smooth Hermitian background h in the local-embedding sense. This means that near every point an embedding into an open set of complex Euclidean space realizes h as the restriction of a smooth strictly positive ambient (1,1)-form. The background is not assumed closed. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Potentials are genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic representatives, locally defined by holomorphic disk tests and canonical upper values. On each holomorphic disk f into X, choose a local smooth real potential p_f with dd^c p_f=f* h; then u composed with f plus p_f is genuine subharmonic or identically minus infinity. A disk contained in a pole set is allowed to have identically-minus-infinity restriction and is not assigned a distributional derivative. The potential u itself is not identically minus infinity on X. Arbitrary null-set modifications are excluded. On a resolution pi:Y->X the extended non-pluripolar measure is computed from pi*h+dd^c(pi*u) upstairs and pushed forward; any claimed equation and singularity class must be independent of common refinements. Ordinary type of a reference psi means u<=psi+C and psi<=u+C for a finite constant C, with genuine canonical extended values, so common poles are interpreted without subtracting minus infinity from minus infinity. For finite positive non-pluripolar Borel data nu, the desired normalized equations have form MA_ext_h(u)=c nu, c>0, sup_X u=0, in a specified genuine singularity type.

Original P23 asks for geometric and measure conditions beyond explicit projective-cone constructions that give finite mass, existence and uniqueness in specified singularity classes, and continuity or regularity downstairs. State the actual singularity class, what continuity means at poles and whether it is the potential or a residual. Solving an equation on a resolution does not itself prove descent: the potential must be constant on its compact fibers with the appropriate canonical values. A pullback background on a resolution, or under a finite map with ramification, may be degenerate and cannot be silently declared positive. State all measure transformations with the original normalization and degree/Jacobian factors. Existing disk-test descent for modifications, resolution-independent products, projective-cone examples, and continuity under existing log-terminal hypotheses are background; merely repeating these does not resolve the request for new conditions. No candidate family, theorem or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_task.completionCriteria: Prove a genuinely new explicit set of sufficient geometric and measure hypotheses with a nontrivial compact example beyond the stated projective-cone cases, giving existence and constant-difference uniqueness within the entire specified singularity class, finite mass and genuinely proved descent/continuity, stable under common refinements. Verify all external theorem hypotheses against primary sources and independently reconstruct the full argument. Expand any positivity or solvability assumptions used, and do not assume the desired existence/uniqueness/continuity as hypotheses. A smooth solution upstairs without descent, uniqueness only among smooth solutions when the type includes rough potentials, a measure formula omitting finite degree or exceptional behavior, or a restatement of an existing log-terminal continuity theorem alone does not meet the task. A proved sufficient-condition theorem must stay scoped; it does not claim a classification of arbitrary unibranch singularities or arbitrary prescribed types.

exact_original_catalogue_text:
2.23    P23: Equations in prescribed types on compact unibranch Hermitian
        spaces
Status: open in the stated generality. Book locator: Problem 32.10.1, printed p. 899.
Setup and scope. Let X be a compact reduced locally irreducible (unibranch) complex space
with a smooth Hermitian background in the local-embedding sense. Potentials are deﬁned by
holomorphic disk tests. On a resolution π : Y → X, extended measures are computed upstairs and
pushed forward; existence in a speciﬁed type also requires the upstairs potential to descend. The
target is a geometric and measure criterion valid beyond explicit projective cones.
Full problem statement. Beyond the projective-cone constructions of Book, Section A.6, deter-
mine geometric and measure conditions on compact unibranch Hermitian spaces that give existence
and uniqueness in speciﬁed singularity classes. Identify estimates ensuring ﬁnite mass, descent and
continuity, and their behavior under common reﬁnements.
State of the art. The appendix proves disk-test descent under modiﬁcations and compatibility of
ordinary envelopes, constructs resolution-independent non-pluripolar products, and gives explicit
equations on projective cones under stated inequalities on their data. Dang provides continuity
for bounded solutions under additional hypotheses, notably a log-terminal setting. Pan constructs
a Gauduchon metric on the regular locus uniformly comparable to the prescribed metric, with
conformal uniqueness up to scale.
Remaining gap. Find assumptions giving ﬁnite mass, existence, uniqueness in the speciﬁed class,
and continuity downstairs, stable under common reﬁnements. Arbitrary unibranch singularities
are not covered by log-terminal results. Scalar bounds and resolution-level regularity do not alone
supply descent or control near the singular locus.
Sources. [22, Theorem B]; [23, Theorems A and A’]; Appendix A, especially Book, Section A.6.


3     Further unresolved questions in the prose
These entries have no formal problem number in the accepted manuscript. Their statements are
explicit formulations of the cited prose, not additional conjectures attributed to an external author.
Overlaps with formal problems are recorded. S18 is a research objective whose precise invariant
still needs formulation.
current_primary_application_judgment: The BT82 decreasing and weighted convergence hypotheses hold after fixed quadratic shifts of canonical bounded torus convolutions and common vanishing constants. The top-degree weighted case is additionally reconstructed by the circular lift in the complete current article. Capacity-zero/pluripolar equivalence and normalized bounded psh sums establish noncharging for mixed products, smooth-background corrections and exceptional loci. BT76 only supplies bounded recursion and its stated continuous-potential limits; it is not substituted for the later discontinuous-limit results. Demailly local integrability applies to connected nontrivial pullbacks of pole witnesses through the degree-one normalization. Every operator rescaling is (4pi)^(-r) for degree r. The already read full relevant primary proofs remain unchanged; no new whole-source reread is claimed.

clause_assessment.request: New geometric and measure conditions beyond projective cones
clause_assessment.answer: Curve theorem: finite bijective torus normalization, any ambient-positive local-embedding background, finite logarithmic ordinary type with total weight below background mass, and normalization-side nonzero nonnegative Lp density p>1. Higher theorem: cuspidally pinched elliptic product in every n>=2, an explicitly nonclosed surface-supported background and full-variable positive H^s data in a quantified normalized perturbative ball. Neither family is a projective cone or log-terminal example.

clause_assessment.request: Actual positivity, solvability and prescribed type
clause_assessment.answer: The rank-deficient normalization background is retained. Fourier primitives explicitly repair it; full-variable polynomial contraction with fixed geometric constants proves higher-dimensional existence. The curve Green solution has precisely the prescribed genuine logarithmic type, and the higher theorem treats the entire bounded ordinary type; existence is not an assumed antecedent.

clause_assessment.request: Finite mass and constant-difference uniqueness among the full specified type
clause_assessment.answer: Curve circular means force every fixed pole atom, leaving mass H-A for every genuine rough competitor; distributional Fourier inversion forces constants. In every higher dimension dd^c closure of all powers fixes every bounded mass M; canonical weighted decreasing products and an energy inequality compare every rough competitor with the constructed positive residual solution.

clause_assessment.request: Descent and continuity with canonical values at singularities or poles
clause_assessment.answer: Finite degree-one cusp normalization is a homeomorphism; every disk has a holomorphic lift. These give actual disk-test descent. Curve residual is a continuous real function across all poles, while the full potential has extended-value continuity there. Higher full bounded potential has ambient Holder exponent 1/3 across the cusp, with C2 regularity upstairs and on the regular locus.

clause_assessment.request: Measure normalization, ramification, degenerate pullback and common refinements
clause_assessment.answer: Degree is one; regular density is f/b in the curve and f/J in higher dimension, with lambda f/rho only in the punctured cusp chart. Zero exceptional mass and literal fiber-constant composed potentials prove every resolution/common-refinement independence. Pullbacks on refinements are never silently declared positive.

scope_assessment: The unchanged original asks for sufficient geometric and measure conditions with all listed consequences. Both complete checked papers supply such theorems; the higher theorem also satisfies the later strengthened arbitrary-dimensional/nonclosed task. The broader classifications expressly left open are not prerequisites for answering this original condition request. This corrects completion accounting without extending either result.
